newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil advances, crude awaits U.S. expiries.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil advances, crude awaits U.S. expiries.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures edged higher on Thursday, playing catch up on energy contract rallies, with crude futures slightly weaker as the market waited to see how New York would react to product expiries.
By 0947 GMT front month gas oil was 75 cents higher at $171.75 a tonne, while Brent was three cents lower at $18.94, just six cents off Wednesday's 8-week $19 high.
"We're just waiting to see what New York gas oil does after the expiries," a broker said. "We're seeing pretty low volume."
NYMEX August unleaded gasoline and heating oil contracts expire on Thursday.
The market was divided as to how New York would react to the expiries.
"It could go either way. We could see some more covering down on the gasoline, or it could all fizzle out."
September Brent closed 38 cents higher on Wednesday at $18.97 a barrel, having earlier touched a high of $19 a barrel.
August gas oil closed $3.25 up on Wednesday at $171 a tonne.

Gas oil and crude on Wednesday advanced on the back of U.S. gasoline, which rallied strongly after U.S. Department of Energy and American Petroleum Institute stock data showed lower than expected gasoline stocks.
"I would expect to see a hesitation and a retracement after the expiry of the front month U.S. products," one broker said. "The market will be keeping a close eye on U.S. gasoline."
Production interruptions and increased demand during the busy summer driving season in the U.S. also helped to boost gasoline.
"I don't think that September will be as strong as the August contract," one broker said. "But I do think we'll start to see September pull away from the rest of the board."
Traders remained cautious ahead of any news on the resumption of Iraqi oil exports under the U.N. food-for-oil deal.
The U.N. was expected to complete its review of the Iraqi aid distribution plan this week.
